title: First Contact Resolution What Is It
summary: The shocking truth: most companies claiming 80% first contact resolution are lying. Here's why your real FCR is probably under 50%—and the exact playbook to fix it without faking the numbers.
body_text: Let me tell you about the metric that nearly every support team lies about. First Contact Resolution (FCR) measures whether you can solve a customer's problem in one shot. No callbacks, no escalations, no "let me get back to you." Just done. Here's the uncomfortable truth: most companies claiming 70-80% FCR rates are measuring it wrong. They count when agents mark tickets "resolved," not when customers actually stop calling back. The real FCR rates? Often below 50%. "We were reporting 82% FCR while our repeat contact rate was 43%," one support director admitted to me last month. FCR isn't just another KPI, it's the mirror that shows whether your support operation actually works or just pretends to. What First Contact Resolution Actually Means FCR happens when a customer contacts you once and walks away with their problem completely solved. Not bandaged. Not escalated. Solved. The key elements that everyone conveniently forgets: Complete resolution from the customer's perspective First interaction only (even if it takes 45 minutes) Works across all channels, phone, chat, email, everything Customer doesn't need to contact you again about the same issue The old "First Call Resolution" metric died when support went omnichannel. Modern FCR doesn't care if customers start on chat and switch to phone. What matters is whether they had to contact you twice. Most companies calculate it wrong. They use this formula: FCR = (Issues resolved on first contact / Total first contacts) × 100. Sounds simple until you realize nobody agrees on what "resolved" means. Why Companies Can't Hit Real FCR Targets SQM Group found that every 1% FCR improvement drives 1% higher satisfaction. Yet most organizations plateau around 71% FCR because they're fighting the wrong battles. The cost reality is brutal. Second contacts cost 2-3 times more than first resolutions. Every repeat ticket doesn't just burn money, it torches customer trust. When someone explains their problem for the third time, they're not just frustrated. They're shopping for your replacement. But here's what nobody discusses: FCR failures destroy your agents too. Support professionals didn't sign up to apologize for systems that don't work. They want to solve problems. When they can't, turnover spikes and hiring costs explode. The Real Barriers Nobody Admits Knowledge gaps kill FCR. Your agents are smart, but they can't access what they need. Product specs live in engineering wikis. Policies hide in legal documents. Account details scatter across five systems. "Our average agent toggled between seven screens per call," according to one study. Authorization theater wastes everyone's time. Agents know the right answer but need supervisor approval for a $20 refund. By the time approval comes, the customer's gone from annoyed to livid. Disconnected systems create disconnected experiences. When your CRM doesn't talk to your billing system, agents become data entry clerks instead of problem solvers. Training focuses on scripts, not solutions. Most programs teach agents what to say, not how to think. They memorize policies instead of understanding problems. The Playbook That Actually Improves FCR Build knowledge management that works. Not another dusty wiki—a living system that agents actually use. The best ones include: Step-by-step troubleshooting guides Searchable, current FAQs Decision trees for complex issues Give agents real power. Set clear limits and let them work within them. Approve refunds up to $100. Allow policy exceptions for loyal customers. Trust them to make judgment calls. Route intelligently from the start. Skills-based routing, pre-chat surveys, and predictive analytics can boost FCR by 23% when implemented correctly. Get the right issue to the right agent immediately. Train for problem-solving, not compliance. Teach agents to diagnose root causes, not just symptoms. Focus on critical thinking over script adherence. Most importantly, train them on every system they'll need, thoroughly. How Technology Changes Everything At Quivr, we built our platform specifically to enable true first contact resolution. Our AI surfaces relevant knowledge instantly. But technology only enables FCR. The real work happens when you commit to measuring honestly, empowering completely, and improving relentlessly. "Make it right the first time" isn't just good service—it's good business. The companies winning tomorrow won't be the ones with the best scripts. They'll be the ones brave enough to measure real resolution and fix what's broken. Your customers already know your true FCR rate. Isn't it time you did too?

title: Gestão de Notas Fiscais (XML): como automatizar a coleta no Cartão PJ
summary: Aprenda a eliminar a digitação manual. Descubra como o Cartão Stark captura o XML de notas fiscais de forma 100% automatizada e integrada por API
body_text: Aprenda a eliminar a digitação manual. Descubra como o Cartão Stark captura o XML de notas fiscais de forma 100% automatizada e integrada por API A gestão de notas fiscais em XML pode se tornar um desafio operacional significativo para times financeiros quando feita de forma manual: horas de retrabalho no fechamento, risco tributário por documentos ausentes e dependência da ação de colaboradores para uma tarefa que deveria ser automática. A boa notícia é que já existem ferramentas que automatizam esse processo inteiramente, eliminando a coleta manual desde o momento da transação. Neste artigo, você descobre como funciona esse modelo, por que ele é crítico para empresas em crescimento e como o Stark Bank resolve esse problema nativamente no cartão corporativo PJ. Confira! O que é gestão de notas fiscais (XML) e por que ela é crítica para empresas A Nota Fiscal Eletrônica (NF-e) é um documento fiscal que existe, juridicamente, apenas em formato eletrônico. Ela é gerada pelo fornecedor, assinada digitalmente e autorizada pela Secretaria da Fazenda (SEFAZ), e é exatamente esse arquivo, no formato XML, que tem validade fiscal plena. Já o DANFE, aquele documento impresso no caixa, ou o PDF que chega por e-mail, é apenas uma representação visual da nota fiscal, útil para consulta rápida, mas sem valor jurídico para escrituração, aproveitamento de créditos ou defesa em auditoria. Para empresas sujeitas ao Lucro Real ou Presumido, uma gestão inadequada das notas fiscais tem consequências importantes: A legislação tributária brasileira exige o armazenamento dos XMLs por, no mínimo, 5 anos (Ajuste SINIEF 07/2005). A ausência do XML original pode inviabilizar o aproveitamento de créditos de PIS, COFINS e ICMS, gerando glosas fiscais. A reconstituição retroativa exige acesso manual ao portal da SEFAZ com a chave de acesso de 44 dígitos de cada nota, um processo que consome horas por lote de documentos. Assim, em empresas com faturamento anual acima de R$ 10 milhões, a gestão inadequada de XMLs deixa de ser uma questão operacional e passa a ser um risco de compliance que impacta diretamente o balanço patrimonial, a DRE (Demonstração de Resultado do Exercício) e os processos de auditoria interna e externa. Como funciona o fluxo tradicional de recebimento e organização de XML No modelo convencional, o XML chega por e-mail do fornecedor, é baixado pelo colaborador, salvo em alguma pasta local ou de rede e só é reenviado ao financeiro quando solicitado. Na prática, esse fluxo pode falhar em várias etapas: O e-mail com o XML vai para spam ou é arquivado sem ação. O colaborador recebe o DANFE em PDF no caixa e não solicita o XML ao fornecedor. O arquivo é salvo no notebook do funcionário e se perde. Fornecedores menores não enviam o XML automaticamente, exigindo consulta manual na SEFAZ. No fechamento, o analista financeiro precisa cruzar o extrato do cartão com os XMLs disponíveis e, para cada um ausente, acessar o portal estadual da SEFAZ com a chave de 44 dígitos. Para uma empresa com 100 transações mensais em cartão corporativo, esse processo consome entre 12 e 20 horas de trabalho de um analista sênior por mês, um custo operacional que raramente aparece nos dashboards de eficiência. O gargalo do reembolso: a ineficiência das notas fiscais em cartões corporativos herdados Os cartões PJ de bancos tradicionais foram desenhados para controle de gastos, não para documentação fiscal. A empresa recebe o extrato, mas a responsabilidade de coletar e organizar os XMLs segue sendo do colaborador ou do financeiro. Os modelos mais comuns, como relatório manual com foto de cupom fiscal, upload periódico em lote ou conciliação retroativa, têm a mesma limitação estrutural: todos transferem para o departamento financeiro o custo de uma ineficiência criada no momento da compra. O problema é que esses modelos tratam a documentação fiscal como um processo de back-office, desconectado do momento em que a transação acontece. O colaborador faz a compra no cartão, e o financeiro descobre a ausência do XML apenas semanas depois, quando a janela de solicitação ao fornecedor já passou ou quando a nota foi cancelada e substituída por outra. O Cartão Corporativo Stark Bank foi desenvolvido a partir de uma premissa diferente: a captura do documento fiscal não pode depender da ação do colaborador, e sim acontecer automaticamente, na origem do pagamento. Integração via API: conectando a recepção de XML aos sistemas de gestão e ao painel Stark Bank A captura automática resolve a coleta. A API do Stark Bank resolve o fluxo: como o documento chega, estruturado e sem intervenção manual, ao ERP que vai processar a escrituração. O payload disponibilizado contém dados da transação em JSON, chave de acesso da NF-e e link de download do XML – compatível com SAP, NetSuite, TOTVS e qualquer sistema que aceite integrações via API REST. Veja na tabela abaixo um comparativo entre o modelo tradicional vs. o modelo Stark Bank: Diferencial Operacional Sistemas Tradicionais Modelo Stark Bank Captura do XML Upload manual pelo colaborador ou envio pelo fornecedor via e-mail Busca ativa automática na SEFAZ associada à transação do cartão Tempo de processamento Dias ou semanas de conferência ao fechamento mensal Segundos: transação e XML conciliados instantaneamente Integração com ERP Digitação de chaves de acesso e conciliação em lote Webhooks e APIs REST com payload JSON estruturado Armazenamento fiscal Risco de perda de arquivos e passivo tributário Guarda eletrônica centralizada para compliance de longo prazo Para empresas que utilizam o cartão virtual corporativo PJ em assinaturas recorrentes, a integração via API associa automaticamente os XMLs dessas transações, eliminando um dos maiores gargalos na conciliação de despesas de software e serviços. Compliance e Reforma Tributária B2B: o impacto das novas regras fiscais na gestão de XML A Reforma Tributária (EC nº 132/2023) substituirá gradualmente os tributos sobre consumo pelo IBS (Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços) e pela CBS (Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços), em implementação progressiva conforme regulamentação complementar. Para o departamento fiscal, o impacto é direto em três frentes: O aproveitamento de créditos no novo modelo dependerá de documentação eletrônica devidamente autorizada, armazenada e conciliada – a mesma lógica que rege o ICMS e o PIS/COFINS hoje, potencialmente com escopo ampliado. A auditoria fiscal cruzada entre NF-es emitidas e declarações das empresas tende a se intensificar, com divergências gerando autuações automáticas sem necessidade de fiscalização presencial. Empresas com XMLs incompletos ou conciliação defasada precisarão corrigir suas bases históricas antes de entrar no novo regime, tornando o saneamento do processo fiscal uma prioridade estratégica de curto prazo. Automatizar a captura de XML hoje é, portanto, tanto uma otimização operacional presente quanto uma medida de preparação para compliance futuro. Empresas que já operam com a base fiscal organizada chegarão à transição tributária em posição significativamente mais vantajosa. Métricas de ROI: quanto a sua empresa economiza ao eliminar o processamento manual Automatizar a captura de documentos fiscais não economiza apenas tempo, como também economiza dinheiro. Cada hora de analista redirecionada do retrabalho contábil para atividades estratégicas tem um custo direto no OPEX do departamento financeiro, e o ROI da automação começa a aparecer já no primeiro fechamento mensal após a migração. Os cenários abaixo ilustram esse impacto com premissas de mercado para departamentos financeiros de médio porte no Brasil. Os resultados reais variam conforme o perfil de gastos e a estrutura da equipe. R$ 80/hora R$ 75/hora Custo mensal do processo manual R$ 3.200/mês R$ 24.000/mês Custo anual do processo manual R$ 38.400/ano R$ 288.000/ano Além do custo direto de horas trabalhadas, há o impacto do risco tributário: estima-se que empresas com gestão manual de XMLs operem com taxas de 5% a 10% de notas não capturadas por mês, o que, em um ticket médio de R$ 800 por transação, pode representar dezenas de milhares de reais anuais em créditos tributários não aproveitados ou em base para autuações. A eliminação desse custo operacional, combinada com a conciliação bancária automatizada , reduz as duas maiores fontes de retrabalho contábil no fechamento mensal. Como começar a centralizar sua gestão fiscal e financeira de alta performance O ponto de entrada é substituir o cartão corporativo do banco tradicional pelo cartão corporativo do Stark Bank, que carrega nativamente a captura automática de XML sem nenhuma configuração adicional para o time financeiro. A integração via API com o sistema de gestão existente pode ser implementada em paralelo, com ambiente de testes disponível antes da entrada em produção. Para o CFO, o impacto é percebido no primeiro fechamento após a migração: a equipe deixa de buscar documentos e passa a validar exceções. Para o time de tecnologia, o Stark Bank disponibiliza documentação técnica detalhada, endpoints padronizados e sandbox para validação completa antes da entrada em produção. O fluxo de onboarding foi desenhado para que a integração com os principais ERPs do mercado seja concluída sem desenvolvimento customizado complexo. Abra sua conta empresarial no Stark Bank e conte com infraestrutura financeira integrada por API para empresas que operam em alta escala. Perguntas frequentes sobre gestão de notas fiscais XML Como o cartão corporativo do Stark Bank captura o arquivo XML automaticamente? O Stark Bank realiza a busca ativa na SEFAZ no momento de cada transação, usando o CNPJ da empresa e os dados do cartão como parâmetros de identificação. O processo não depende do envio do XML pelo fornecedor via e-mail nem de ação do colaborador; a captura ocorre de forma autônoma e o arquivo fica disponível no painel e via API em segundos. Qual o risco fiscal de não realizar a gestão adequada de XMLs de compras PJ? A ausência dos arquivos XML expõe a empresa a glosas fiscais no aproveitamento de créditos de PIS, COFINS e ICMS, impossibilidade de reconstituição em caso de fiscalização e autuações por divergência com os registros da SEFAZ. A legislação exige armazenamento por no mínimo 5 anos, e o cruzamento eletrônico de dados pela Receita Federal está cada vez mais automatizado. body_text: Share With the right fleet management solution many manual processes and workflows are removed. Furthermore, deploying the right solution gives you visibility into everything you need your eyes on operationally. You’ll make more informed decisions, save time and money, and improve driver safety. In this article we cover everything you need to know about the best fleet management tools. We share some brief refreshers, important features to look for, and the benefits of partnering with a provider with expertise in fleet fueling, charging, and related expense management. Download the Fleet management: A complete guide white paper Get access to impactful insights and an overall guide to how to best manage your fleet. Read now A brief refresher on fleet management Fleet management involves overseeing and coordinating one or more company vehicles to ensure efficiency, safety, and cost-effectiveness across an organization — from small businesses to large enterprises. These days, the range of off-the-shelf fleet management products is broad. There are effective, time-tested solutions specifically designed for fleet expense management which provide the best operational efficiency for your business, no matter the size. Larger businesses and those at the enterprise level likely have one, if not multiple, fleet managers who oversee operations. Fleet management solutions and systems augment fleet managers’ jobs by streamlining things like data collection, tracking, and fuel management. Typically, to be an effective fleet manager, you have visibility into various aspects of driver behavior, vehicle health, etc. — and tools that can provide it. In most cases, this means oversight of: Vehicle tracking: GPS technology helps monitor vehicle location, route efficiency, and overall fleet movement to help keep track of drivers, mitigate fraud, and reduce vehicle misuse. Fuel management: Monitoring fuel consumption and optimizing routes helps to reduce fuel costs and the environmental impact of your fleet. Driver training/management: Monitoring driver behavior, ensuring compliance with regulations, and providing training when needed contribute to overall fleet safety and efficiency. Safety and compliance: Ensuring that vehicles comply with safety standards and regulatory requirements helps avoid legal issues and enhances overall safety. Data analytics and reporting: Using data analytics to gain insights into fleet performance and generating robust reports helps in myriad ways, from enhanced decision-making to better driver training. Telematics: Integrating telematics technology into your fleet operations makes it easier to collect and analyze data related to vehicle performance, driver behavior, and other relevant factors overseen by fleet managers. What kind of organizations require robust fleet management? Fleet management and related solutions aren’t reserved for multi-million dollar enterprises. Small businesses, even those with just one or a handful of fleet vehicles, benefit from well-integrated management solutions. The following industries are examples that commonly have a dedicated fleet manager, whose job it is to ensure operations are running smoothly, as expected, and as efficiently as possible: Transportation and logistics companies Delivery companies Public transportation services Utility companies Government and municipalities Waste management Car rental companies Healthcare organizations Small business owners Challenges that fleet managers face Across all industries and business sizes, fleet managers face challenges that can be difficult to overcome without the right tools and insight: Vehicle downtime: Unplanned downtime, which sometimes leads to unscheduled maintenance, can increase your operating costs. While it’s tricky to nail down the average cost of unplanned downtime, you can make an informed guess by summing the hourly cost of a driver and hourly profit loss. If the vehicle also needs maintenance, you’ll have to spend even more. Regulatory compliance: Fleet vehicles are held to a litany of standards and regulations set forth by federal and state authorities, which can be tough to maintain without proper visibility into operations. Fleet maintenance: Another large — and expensive — hurdle in fleet management, maintenance bills can add up quickly and unexpectedly. Using tools like GPS tracking and telematics, fleet managers can keep track of their vehicles to know when they need service. Driver behavior: Poor driving habits increase the chances of collisions, injuries, and even death. Not only do poor habits like harsh braking and idling wear down vehicles faster or consume more fuel than necessary, but they can also lead to lawsuits and increased insurance premiums that your business will be responsible for paying. Fleet management solutions: Overview and benefits Fleet management partners have the expertise and tools to streamline and optimize the various tasks associated with effectively managing a fleet of vehicles — big or small. Typically, a robust fleet management solution offers a centralized platform for monitoring, controlling, and analyzing all aspects of your fleet operations, from driver behavior to fuel usage. When searching for a fleet partner, there are several integral offerings you should be on the lookout for: GPS tracking and telematics Maintenance scheduling tools Fuel card programs Driver performance monitoring GPS vehicle tracking Premium GPS tracking for your fleet provides real-time visibility into the location and movement of each vehicle. Fleet managers can use the information gathered via GPS to discern poor driving habits and take corrective action, monitor and mitigate instances of fraud and vehicle misuse, and drive down fleet operations spending across the board. Maintenance scheduling and alerts Fleet management solutions that offer GPS tracking and a centralized dashboard for vehicle analytics make scheduling and tracking regular maintenance tasks easier to reduce the risk of breakdowns and extend the lifespan of vehicles. Fuel management and fuel cards Fuel cards are an invaluable aspect of fleet management — especially for growing businesses. With the right card, you should get automatic fuel expense tracking, a robust set of employee controls and alerts, rebates that create a brand-new revenue stream, and more. An effective fleet fuel card should offer features such as: Transaction monitoring: Real-time tracking of fuel transactions allows for better oversight, helping fleet managers identify irregularities or unauthorized purchases. Customized reporting: Generate detailed reports on fuel usage, spending patterns, and other relevant metrics. Access to a large fuel station network: 95% of all retail fuel locations in the United States accept the WEX fuel card, providing drivers with convenient options. Usage controls: Set restrictions on card usage, such as limiting the type of fuel purchased, the number of transactions, and spending limits to prevent misuse. Integration: Seamlessly integrate WEX fuel card data with GPS and telematics analytics for complete visibility into driver performance, transactions, vehicle usage, and more. Driver performance monitoring Using a combination of data gathered from onboard GPS telematics and an integrated fuel card, you can keep tabs on driver behavior, from driving performance to spending habits, to help improve safety and reduce fuel fraud. Premium tracking features should provide insight into driver behavior. This includes: Speed Idling time Harsh braking On the payment side, get clarity and alerts based on spending so you know when drivers may be exhausting limits or stealing fuel. With the right fleet partner, you’ll be able to promote safer driving practices and may even lower your insurance costs over time. Compliance and regulatory management Overseeing commercial vehicles means overseeing many compliance requirements. The best fleet management solutions can help keep your operation organized and in compliance. For example, in the event of a regulatory audit, fleet management solutions provide accurate and organized data via telematics tracking. Stored and easily accessible historical information makes it easier for organizations to demonstrate compliance during audits. Furthermore, many regions have strict regulations regarding the maximum hours a driver can operate a vehicle within a specific timeframe. GPS tracking and telematics monitor and log driver hours automatically, ensuring hours of service (HOS) compliance . Telematics integration Telematics opens a window into vehicle performance, which is essential for monitoring engine diagnostics and assessing overall fleet efficiency. Using the data gathered from vehicle telematics, fleet managers can: Best manage route optimization Keep a finger on the pulse of vehicle health Have a proactive approach to maintenance and scheduling Help reduce downtime and prevent costly repairs Customizable dashboards and reports Fuel card providers also allow users to create customized dashboards and reports based on their specific needs, providing a comprehensive overview of fleet performance. What’s more, WEX enables preventive maintenance scheduling to minimize downtime and reduce overall operational costs for your fleet. With the easy and free integration of fuel cards and telematics data, fleet managers can more easily analyze driver behavior and fuel consumption to foster a culture of responsible driving. WEX speaks the language of small business operators. title: The DMA should not undercut security & privacy for Europeans
summary: Today's decisions risk undermining vital privacy and security guardrails for millions of Europeans. We have repeatedly offered solutions to safeguard users while satisfy…
body_text: Today's decisions risk undermining vital privacy and security guardrails for millions of Europeans. We have repeatedly offered solutions to safeguard users while satisfying the DMA's goals, but these rulings discount extensive evidence of user harm. The reality is that AI assistants already safely access Android’s capabilities, with phone makers playing a key role in vetting them. This Android ruling threatens device security by granting external apps sensitive and powerful device permissions without these safeguards. This is occurring as the EU’s own cybersecurity agency warns that “security fundamentals matter more than ever in the age of AI”. Of particular concern, Europeans’ private searches would be exposed to unfamiliar companies, without adequate anonymisation of the data and without user knowledge or consent. This would weaken citizens' privacy, risk business trade secrets, and endanger national security. As the Commission's decision recognises, a flexible, evidence-based process will be critical to account for these significant harms and adjust measures accordingly. We will continue advocating for a balanced approach that protects privacy and security while supporting market goals.

body_text: Aziende di ogni dimensione si sono affidate ad Amazon Business per i suoi strumenti basati sull’intelligenza artificiale, per l’ampia selezione di prodotti, i prezzi competitivi, le soluzioni di consegna e i vantaggi dell'abbonamento Prime Business. Più di 1,8 milioni di nuove aziende hanno scelto Amazon Business dall'inizio dell'anno. Milano, 21 luglio 2026 – Amazon Business ha raggiunto 60 miliardi di dollari di vendite lorde annualizzate nel secondo trimestre, aiutando oltre 11 milioni di organizzazioni in tutto il mondo a semplificare i propri acquisti aziendali. Organizzazioni di ogni dimensione - dagli ospedali alle scuole, dalle fabbriche agli hotel - utilizzano Amazon Business per acquistare ciò di cui hanno bisogno per operare. Dal lancio negli Stati Uniti nel 2015, Amazon Business è cresciuto fino a servire organizzazioni in 11 Paesi, tra cui centinaia di migliaia di piccole imprese e 97 delle 100 aziende Fortune 100. Nella prima metà del 2026, più di 1,8 milioni di nuove organizzazioni hanno aderito ad Amazon Business, accelerando ulteriormente questa crescita. Le organizzazioni stanno ripensando il modo in cui acquistano, cercando un'esperienza che offra la stessa semplicità dello shopping personale, ma progettata per il contesto lavorativo. Amazon Business ha sviluppato un'offerta che combina il meglio di entrambi i mondi: ampia selezione, esperienza di acquisto e di consegna progettata per le aziende, prezzi bassi e strumenti che consentono alle organizzazioni di controllare gli acquisti e monitorare la spesa. Nell'ultimo anno, Amazon Business ha introdotto nuovi strumenti e servizi progettati per rendere gli acquisti aziendali più semplici e intelligenti, tra cui: Nuovi strumenti basati sull'intelligenza artificiale per aiutare le organizzazioni a individuare opportunità di risparmio. Espansione della selezione di prodotti rilevanti per il business grazie a una rete di milioni di venditori. Offerta di prezzi competitivi, prezzi esclusivi per aziende e sconti per quantità. Introduzione di nuovi vantaggi all'interno dell'abbonamento Prime Business. "Aziende di ogni dimensione scelgono Amazon Business per l’ampia selezione di prodotti, la convenienza quotidiana e la rapidità e affidabilità delle consegne. Una fiducia che continua a tradursi in una continua crescita. In un contesto in cui le organizzazioni sono chiamate a fare sempre di più con risorse limitate, continuiamo a innovare per aiutarle a risparmiare tempo e denaro, consentendo loro di reinvestire queste risorse nella crescita del proprio business." Geraldine Valenti Director Amazon Business Francia, Italia e Spagna Strumenti basati sull'Intelligenza Artificiale per individuare opportunità di risparmio Gli acquirenti aziendali di oggi apprezzano un’esperienza personalizzata e intuitiva. Amazon Business ha introdotto una serie di strumenti basati sull'intelligenza artificiale progettati per soddisfare questa aspettativa, aiutando le organizzazioni a risparmiare e prendere decisioni di acquisto più intelligenti. Amazon Business Assistant risponde in tempo reale alle domande degli utenti, fornisce supporto sull'account e suggerisce modalità più efficienti di acquisto sulla base della cronologia degli ordini. Savings Insights analizza la spesa aziendale e propone opportunità di risparmio, come sconti per acquisti in grandi quantità o ordini ricorrenti. Spend Anomaly Monitoring avvisa i team quando vengono rilevati acquisti insoliti, aiutando a identificare errori o spese eccessive prima che diventino un problema. Un assortimento in crescita per ogni organizzazione Dalle scuole alle aziende manifatturiere, fino alle officine meccaniche, le aziende cercano sempre più una soluzione d'acquisto centralizzata che consenta di reperire tutto il necessario attraverso un numero ridotto di fornitori. Oggi i clienti Amazon Business hanno accesso a centinaia di milioni di prodotti in tutto il mondo, con un assortimento cresciuto di quasi il 25% rispetto allo stesso periodo dell'anno scorso. Le categorie maggiormente in crescita includono utensili per la manutenzione, mobili per ufficio e prodotti alimentari freschi. Questa offerta è alimentata da una rete di milioni di venditori in tutto il mondo, molti dei quali sono piccole e medie imprese. Amazon Business continua, inoltre, a semplificare la navigazione dell'assortimento attraverso strumenti come Guided Buying , che indirizza i dipendenti verso prodotti preferenziali. Prezzi convenienti e risparmi concreti Quando le organizzazioni spendono meno per ciò di cui hanno bisogno, possono destinare più risorse alla crescita del proprio business. Amazon Business offre prezzi bassi tutto l’anno, prezzi riservati alle aziende e sconti quantitativi su milioni di prodotti. Nel 2025, gli sconti specifici di Amazon Business hanno consentito alle organizzazioni di risparmiare oltre 1 miliardo di dollari a livello globale, dalle scuole che acquistano materiale didattico alle catene alberghiere che riforniscono biancheria e prodotti per la pulizia. Ulteriori risparmi sono possibili attraverso il programma Iscriviti & Risparmia per gli acquisti ricorrenti. Maggiore valore per le attività quotidiane con Prime Business Così come Prime semplifica gli acquisti quotidiani per i consumatori, Prime Business è progettato per fare lo stesso per le aziende. Lo scorso anno i clienti Prime Business hanno risparmiato oltre 880 milioni di dollari nelle spese di spedizione a livello globale. Amazon Business continua a migliorare l’abbonamento introducendo nuovi vantaggi a supporto delle attività aziendali. Lo scorso mese è stato aggiunto Amazon Quick , un assistente personale basato sull'IA che aiuta le persone a lavorare in modo più efficiente. Quick si connette agli strumenti e ai dati già utilizzati in azienda, apprende le priorità dell'utente e può svolgere attività personalizzate come pianificare riunioni, creare documenti o generare dashboard, il tutto sfruttando la sicurezza e la governance aziendale offerte da AWS. Questi vantaggi ampliati possono aiutare le piccole e medie imprese a risparmiare quasi 1.100 dollari all'anno. Informazioni su Amazon Business Amazon Business aiuta milioni di clienti in tutto il mondo a ridisegnare gli acquisti aziendali per risparmiare tempo e denaro. Inoltre, Amazon Business aiuta le aziende ad aumentare la produttività grazie ad analisi degli acquisti basate su dati approfonditi. Imprese di tutte le dimensioni utilizzano Amazon Business: da piccole imprese, scuole, ospedali, organizzazioni no profit e agenzie governative, fino a multinazionali che operano a livello globale. I responsabili degli acquisti aziendali cercano opzioni di consegna convenienti per milioni di prodotti appartenenti a diverse categorie come elettronica, pulizia professionale, alimentari e consumabili, e prodotti per ufficio. I clienti hanno anche accesso a una varietà di funzionalità e vantaggi dedicati alle aziende: fatturazione semplificata, prezzi dedicati alle aziende, sconti sulle quantità, account aziendali singoli o multiutente, flussi di approvazione personalizzabili, integrazione dei sistemi di acquisto, diversi metodi di pagamento, servizio clienti dedicato e molto altro. Amazon Business è attualmente disponibile in Canada, Stati Uniti, Regno Unito, Germania, Francia, Italia, Spagna, Giappone e India. Per ulteriori informazioni, è possibile visitare il sito business.amazon.it , business.amazon.it/blog e seguire @AmazonBusiness .

title: FedEx Named Top Logistics Provider in Asia Pacific at 2026 AFLAS Awards
body_text: Buay Beng Tan (Left), Vice President, Operations, FedEx China, receives the ‘Best Logistics Service Provider - Express’ award from Mr. Lawrence Yam (Right), Commercial Director of Hutchison Ports South China, at the 2026 Asian Freight, Logistics and Supply Chain (AFLAS) Awards ceremony Singapore, July 2, 2026 — Federal Express Corporation, one of the world’s largest express transportation companies, has been named the Best Logistics Service Provider at the 2026 Asian Freight, Logistics and Supply Chain (AFLAS) Awards ceremony held in Shanghai, China. The AFLAS Awards are among the region’s most respected industry accolades, decided by 15,000 participants of logistics professionals, customers and service users. This recognition reflects strong market confidence in the company’s capabilities and its consistent delivery of high-quality service in a highly competitive landscape. “This award is a testament to the trust our customers place in us every day, as well as the dedication of our team members in the region,” said Salil Chari, president, Asia Pacific, FedEx. “We are proud to be recognized by the industry we serve. As global trade becomes more interconnected and supply chains grow more complex, we are combining our global network with data, AI-driven insights, to deliver a smarter logistics ecosystem, helping customers operate with greater visibility, precision, and resilience.” This recognition comes amid strong shifts in regional trade. Across Asia Pacific, trade is becoming faster, more complex, and increasingly regional. As the region leads global trade growth in 2026[1], FedEx is strengthening a data-enabled logistics network that connects key markets and supports high-value industries - automotive, aerospace, semiconductors, manufacturing, electronics, and life sciences - underpinned by continued investment in connectivity and digital capabilities. The award was presented at the AFLAS Awards ceremony held in Shanghai, bringing together leading players from across freight, logistics and supply chain industry. [1] https://www.globaltrademag.com/wto-forecast-global-trade-growth-to-slow-to-1-9-in-2026-amid-conflict-risks/

title: Remote Temperature Monitoring for Foodservice | BOHA! Sense
summary: BOHA! Sense monitors temperature and humidity in coolers, freezers and walk-ins 24/7, alerting teams before drift becomes food loss or a safety risk.
body_text: Spoilage risk often starts before anyone sees it A cooler running a few degrees warm. A freezer taking longer to recover after a delivery. A walk-in whose humidity has been creeping up overnight. None of these looks like a failure, and in a busy kitchen they are easy to miss until product quality slips or someone asks what the temperature logs actually show. BOHA! Sense is a remote temperature and humidity monitoring system for foodservice equipment: refrigerators, freezers, walk-ins, and dry storage. Wireless sensors track conditions around the clock and alert the team when a piece of equipment drifts out of its normal range, so someone can respond before a small change turns into food loss, a food safety risk, or costly equipment repair, even worse replacement. It does not replace people or maintenance, it enhances response time and awareness. BOHA! Sense enables earlier, more consistent visibility versus a single manual check at one point in the day, so problems are easier to catch, investigate, and document. What is BOHA! Sense? BOHA! Sense pairs small, rugged wireless sensors with a gateway that gathers data, sending it to the BOHA! platform, accessible via the BOHA! Sense mobile app on iOS or Android, and the BOHA! Control Center. The sensors sit inside refrigerators, freezers, walk-ins, and dry storage and report temperature and humidity continuously, day and night. What it brings to the kitchen: Round-the-clock monitoring of temperature and humidity across refrigerators, freezers, walk-ins, and dry storage Alerts and notifications the moment equipment moves out of its normal range, at any hour Wireless LoRaWAN sensors with long range, and better penetrability in areas with limited connectivity, like walk-ins fridges, freezers, and other heavy equipment and cold storage Rugged, IP65-rated sensors with long, replaceable battery life, built for kitchen conditions Temperature accuracy to within ±0.4°C and humidity to within ±3% RH, with onboard logging of up to 10,000 measurements Setup in minutes, no drilling required, using the BOHA! Gateway and sensors One point on scope, because it matters: BOHA! Sense monitors temperature and humidity conditions to keep product safe. What it gives a team is real-time visibility into how their refrigerated environments are behaving, so they know when something moves out of range. It won’t solve the problems by itself, but makes the problems visible, allowing teams to take action sooner and ensure product remains high quality and food safe for patrons. How earlier detection supports waste reduction and food safety Waste and spoilage reduction depends on catching problems early enough to respond. BOHA! Sense gives users that early warning. It makes equipment conditions visible so teams can act, moving product, checking equipment, or escalating, before spoilage spreads and costs rise. Over time, equipment monitoring visibility helps operators reduce the avoidable food loss that can quietly and quickly kill quality and drive up food costs. The same visibility supports food safety and compliance. Continuous temperature and humidity records show whether refrigeration, freezer, walk-in, and storage conditions stayed within expected ranges; and, when corrective action is needed, it’s done promptly and recorded, strengthening food safety documentation and audit readiness. Sense data rounds out the picture alongside BOHA! Temp and the wider visibility a multi-location team gets through Control Center. Where temperature and humidity control earns its keep The value tends to show up initially in the moments when manual checks miss. A busy service has the fridge door open for long periods of time, resulting in more food on tables, but also an overworked and overheating refrigerator. This will affect costly and sensitive items like fruit and vegetables, but it could get way worse if the problem persists. With Sense, a walk-in cooler that drifts warm overnight can be flagged before the morning crew arrives. A drink fridge that recovers slowly after a big delivery shows a pattern worth investigating. A reach-in near a hot line that keeps running warm will not keep food at optimal freshness and may point to a failing compressor rather than a placement problem. And across many locations, an issue that looks like a one-off at a single store can turn out to be an operational pattern worth investigating. This kind of refrigeration monitoring , backed by a history of readings, helps teams tell whether a problem is isolated, recurring, or spreading. Earlier visibility can surface behaviors, like doors left open during a rush, that put extra strain on equipment over time, so teams can address them sooner. The real cost of late detection When a refrigerator, freezer, or walk-in drifts out of range, the cost rarely stops with the food inside it. First, there is the product that may need to be discarded. Then there is the replacement of food inventory, the labor spent checking and moving product, the service call and cost of repair (or worse, replacement), and the operational disruption if a menu item, grab-and-go case, prep station, or production schedule is affected. Together, those costs can turn a refrigeration issue into a four- or five-figure operational event. FDA food safety guidance underscores how quickly perishable food becomes a discard risk when refrigeration is interrupted, while commercial refrigeration repair estimates often put major walk-in repairs, such as compressor replacement, in the low-thousands range. Add discarded product, replacement inventory, emergency service, labor, lost sales, and customer impact, and a downed walk-in can reasonably become a $5,000 to $20,000+ incident depending on inventory value, downtime, and operating volume. That’s why real-time refrigeration monitoring has become an important part of how foodservice teams reduce risk before small equipment issues become larger operational costs. In some cases, teams may also need to document what happened, when it happened, and what corrective action was taken. That cost stack can include: Food loss from product that can no longer be used Repurchasing inventory, sometimes on short notice Labor spent inspecting, moving, documenting, or discarding product Emergency repair costs or equipment replacement planning Lost sales if affected items cannot be prepared, stocked, or served Customer experience issues when availability or quality slips BOHA! Sense provides visibility into the health of your equipment and helps teams stay ahead of changes before they turn into major problems. When teams know that a cooler is drifting warm, a freezer is recovering slowly, or a storage area is moving outside its expected range, they have a better chance to act before the issue becomes more expensive. For multi-location operators, that visibility matters even more. One equipment issue at one location is a store-level problem. The same pattern across many locations can point to training gaps, equipment placement issues, door-open behavior, maintenance needs, or broader operational risk. Industry context: refrigeration issues can scale quickly Large operators are also under more pressure to understand and document how large, food safety-dependent systems and equipment, like refrigeration, are performing. In 2026, Grocery Dive reported that Kroger agreed to pay a $2.5 million civil penalty and spend $100 million over three years to retrofit or replace 600 refrigeration units as part of a proposed settlement involving refrigerant leaks and Clean Air Act compliance. BOHA! Sense isn’t a refrigerant leak detector. But the Kroger case is a useful reminder that refrigeration-related issues can become major operational and financial problems when they are hard to detect early, track consistently, or address before they escalate, especially over a distributed network of locations. At scale, refrigeration visibility, maintenance, and documentation are not just store-level concerns – they become enterprise-level issues. BOHA! Sense vs. BOHA! Temp: monitoring equipment vs. checking food It’s worth drawing a clean line between two BOHA! tools that both deal with temperature and food safety but solve different problems. BOHA! Sense monitors the environment. It tracks equipment and the conditions that keep food fresh: the temperature and humidity inside refrigerators, freezers, walk-ins, and storage, around the clock to make sure optimal conditions are maintained to keep food fresh. BOHA! Temp supports active food temperature checks. It supports staff in their daily food safety workflows with active food temperature checks, corrective actions, and audit-ready HACCP records. In simple terms: BOHA! Sense and BOHA! Temp work together. Sense watches the food storage conditions, and Temp guides and documents the checks on the food itself. Operational Need BOHA! Tool Always-on temperature and humidity monitoring of equipment BOHA! Sense Alerts when a fridge, freezer, or walk-in drifts out of range BOHA! Sense Guided food safety processes, recommended corrective actions and HACCP records on demand BOHA! Temp Operational checklists, workflows, and task verification BOHA! Checklist Prep, date-code, and grab-and-go labeling BOHA! T2 or WorkStation Receipts and tickets at the order counter or back-of-house station Ithaca 9000 Best fit for BOHA! Sense BOHA! Sense is best suited for operators who want continuous visibility into the equipment that helps keep food safe, rather than relying only on distracting, time consuming, manual checks at various points in the day. BOHA! Sense can be a strong fit for teams that need: Continuous temperature and humidity monitoring of refrigerators, freezers, walk-ins, and dry storage Alerts when equipment drifts out of range, day or night, including after hours A history of readings to tell whether an issue is isolated, recurring, or spreading across locations Earlier warning that helps reduce avoidable food loss and spoilage Equipment condition history that supports stronger food safety documentation and audit ready HACCP reporting on demand Wireless sensors that install in minutes and hold up in rugged kitchen environments Sense adds a monitoring layer to the BOHA! hardware portfolio. Where BOHA! T2, WorkStation, and the Ithaca 9000 handle printing and labeling workflows, Sense keeps an eye on the equipment and conditions that affect food quality, food safety, spoilage risk, equipment status, and operational continuity. Next in the BOHA! Built series BOHA! Sense watches equipment conditions in the background. But food safety also depends on active checks, corrective actions, and records that hold up during an inspection. Next in BOHA! Built, we look at BOHA! Temp and how temperature workflows support audit readiness. Frequently asked questions about BOHA! Sense These questions cover what BOHA! Sense monitors and how it fits alongside BOHA! Temp. What is BOHA! Sense? BOHA! Sense is a temperature and humidity monitoring system for foodservice equipment, including refrigerators, freezers, walk-ins, and dry storage. Wireless sensors track conditions around the clock and alert the team when equipment moves out of range, so they can respond before food loss or a food safety issue escalates. Does BOHA! Sense detect refrigerant leaks? No. BOHA! Sense is not a refrigerant leak detector, and it does not replace HVAC/R service or maintenance. It monitors temperature and humidity, and alerts teams when conditions move out of range so they can investigate the cause. What is the difference between BOHA! Sense and BOHA! Temp? BOHA! Sense monitors equipment temperature and humidity continuously. BOHA! Temp supports active, daily food temperature checks, corrective actions, and audit-ready HACCP records. Sense watches the storage environment; Temp documents the checks on the food itself. Many operations use both. How does BOHA! Sense help reduce food waste and spoilage? It does not save food on its own. By alerting teams when refrigerators, freezers, or walk-ins drift out of range, and by building a history of conditions, BOHA! Sense helps teams respond earlier, moving product, checking equipment, or escalating, before spoilage spreads and drives up food cost. What equipment can BOHA! Sense monitor? Refrigerators, freezers, walk-in coolers and freezers, and dry storage areas. Wireless LoRaWAN sensors reach through heavy metal storage, and each reports temperature and humidity to the BOHA! app on iOS or Android.

title: Blog | ICAO approves two new CORSIA programmes | Abatable
summary: Understand what ICAO's approvals mean for new CORSIA eligible carbon credit supply in our blog article.
body_text: The Forest Carbon Partnership Facility (FCPF) and the BioCarbon Fund Initiative for Sustainable Forest Landscapes (ISFL) , both World Bank programmes, have been added to the approved list for CORSIA’s First Phase following the latest recommendations from CORSIA’s Technical Advisory Body (TAB). To mirror, or transfer? The TAB’s position on national carbon registries established under the Paris Agreement’s Article 6.2 are also set out in the recommendations. National registries that simply mirror data from CORSIA-approved programme registries are considered broadly acceptable. However, national registries where units are physically transferred from eligible programme registries will likely require greater scrutiny of their processes by the TAB before being approved. The EU weighs in Meanwhile, the European Commission has proposed EU-specific criteria for CORSIA-eligible units used by European airlines. Its proposal, which is early stage and subject to further consultation, would exclude High Forest Low Deforestation (HFLD) credits, certain cookstove credits, and insert specific provisions around first transfer within a Letter of Authorisation. For CORSIA’s Second Phase, only Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism (PACM) units, or credits from programmes demonstrably aligned with PACM standards, would qualify under the Commission’s proposal. Its own estimate – that 90-100% of currently eligible supply would be excluded for EU airlines under First Phase criteria – points to a significant supply constraint for European carriers if this direction holds. Abatable’s angle While a positive development for CORSIA, the newly approved supply is more limited than headline registry figures suggest. The FCPF registry currently lists 15 projects, but only seven have issued credits that could become eligible today, totalling 41.3mn tonnes. This is more than double the volume of CORSIA eligible emissions units (EEUs) currently on registries, however none of this volume holds a government Letter of Authorisation or Corresponding Adjustment – requirements for CORSIA – so whether it would have a material supply impact remains to be seen. Of the host countries with FCPF projects, Ghana, Laos, and Madagascar score highest on Abatable’s Article 6 readiness index, making them the most plausible near-term sources of authorised volume. ISFL’s three projects remain under development with no issued volume, meaning they are some way away from contributing CORSIA-eligible supply. If authorised, these volumes would bring meaningful portfolio diversification. Current EEU supply is heavily skewed: the majority of projects by number are cookstoves, but the dominant source of units by volume is Guyana’s ART TREES programme. FCPF volumes would therefore allow airlines to broaden the composition of their offset portfolios, an approach some may take as a risk mitigation opportunity. On TAB’s clarifications on national registries, the most immediate impact falls on several developers in Zimbabwe, who have cancelled their issued units on Gold Standard and transferred to the Zimbabwean national registry launched last year. This volume was then reissued on the Zimbabwean registry, given a unique serial number, and granted an authorisation for use towards CORSIA. TAB’s guidance means work must be done to ensure the integration and processes of tracking unit cancellation, transfer and issuance before these units can become EEUs. More broadly, as governments develop national registries to track carbon units for Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) and Article 6 accounting, these new guidelines may influence the technical approach they take to registry design.
